title: Harris’s 2003 campaign settlement and the nine payments to the City

beats.text: In 2003, San Francisco changed where candidates had to file their spending pledge.

visual.sub: A midcampaign rule change required a second filing

beats.text: Kamala Harris’s campaign reported spending $91,446 above the district attorney ceiling.

visual.label: The spending statement exceeded the ceiling by $91,446

beats.text: The official voter guide still said she had accepted that ceiling.

visual.kicker: The spending statement exceeded the ceiling by $91,446

beats.text: The commission described the violations as apparently unintentional.

visual.kicker: The spending statement exceeded the ceiling by $91,446

beats.text: The signed settlement has a handwritten change.

visual.kicker: Handwritten changes set one $34,000 cap for two remedies

beats.text: Its $34,000 cap covered both a penalty and corrective publicity.

visual.kicker: Handwritten changes set one $34,000 cap for two remedies

beats.text: The campaign’s reports show nine payments to the City totaling $19,306.

visual.label: City stipulation payments on Schedule E

beats.text: Its final installment schedule shows a zero balance.

visual.kicker: Nine campaign payments to the City total $19,306

beats.text: The records leave the amounts paid to publish the corrections unresolved.

visual.kicker: Nine campaign payments to the City total $19,306

beats.text: A court upheld lifting the spending limit for the November 2003 race.

visual.kicker: The court upheld a separate decision about the whole race
